---
title: "Logistic and Discriminant Methods"
---

This lecture shifts from continuous outcomes to classification and
introduces probability models for class membership.

## Learning Objectives

- Explain why linear regression is not ideal for binary outcomes.
- Fit and interpret logistic regression.
- Compare logistic regression with LDA and QDA.
- Evaluate classifiers using confusion matrices, sensitivity,
  specificity, ROC curves, and calibration.

## Core Ideas

Logistic regression models conditional class probabilities through the
log odds:

$$
\log\left(\frac{p(x)}{1 - p(x)}\right) = x^\top \beta.
$$

Discriminant analysis instead models the distribution of predictors
within each class and then applies Bayes' rule.

## Logistic Regression

For a binary outcome, logistic regression models the probability of the
positive class:

$$
p(x) = \Pr(Y = 1 \mid X = x).
$$

The logit link keeps fitted probabilities between 0 and 1:

$$
p(x) = \frac{\exp(x^\top\beta)}{1 + \exp(x^\top\beta)}.
$$

Coefficients are changes in log odds. Exponentiating a coefficient gives
an odds ratio, holding other predictors fixed.

```r
library(ISLR)

fit <- glm(
  default ~ student + balance + income,
  data = ISLR::Default,
  family = binomial
)

summary(fit)
exp(coef(fit))
```

## LDA and QDA

LDA and QDA start from class-conditional densities,
$f_k(x) = p(X = x \mid Y = k)$, and combine them with class priors
$\pi_k$:

$$
\Pr(Y = k \mid X = x)
= \frac{\pi_k f_k(x)}{\sum_{\ell} \pi_\ell f_\ell(x)}.
$$

LDA assumes a common covariance matrix across classes, producing linear
decision boundaries. QDA allows class-specific covariance matrices,
producing quadratic boundaries.

## Evaluation

Classification accuracy is often not enough, especially with rare
events. Inspect the confusion matrix, sensitivity, specificity, ROC
curve, and calibration. Thresholds should reflect the cost of false
positives and false negatives.

## Classification Comparison

Use a binary classification data set to compare logistic regression,
LDA, and QDA. Emphasize probability estimation before hard class labels.

## Threshold Practice

Practice by fitting logistic regression, LDA, and QDA to the same
classification data. Compare confusion matrices, error rates, and
class probabilities. Explain how the preferred model would change if
false positives and false negatives had different costs.
